Compare Fractions

FractionsArithmeticDivisibility
Game: Two fractions are drawn as boxes so you can see which is bigger; there is nothing to win or lose.
How to play: Press the top half of a digit to raise it and the bottom half to lower it, or use the Up and Down keys. Use the buttons to give both fractions the same bottom number, or to make them as small as they go.
Look for the math

Which is bigger, 3/4 or 5/7? The pictures show a fraction as boxes, but a picture is slow when the numbers get big. There is a faster test that needs only whole-number multiplication.

Compare by subtracting

Two numbers are compared by their difference: the first is bigger exactly when the difference is positive. Put both fractions over a common denominator and subtract:

p/q − r/s = (p·s − r·q) / (q·s)

Cross multiplication

Since q·s is positive, the sign of the answer is the sign of the top: p/q > r/s exactly when p·s > r·q. The status line shows that comparison for the fractions on screen. The logic test checked it against an exact comparison for every pair of fractions with numerators and denominators up to 30 (810,000 pairs) and it never failed.

The two buttons

Common denominator gives both fractions the denominator q·s / gcd(q, s), the least common multiple; the test confirmed that is the smallest possible for all 9,801 pairs of denominators up to 99. Simplify divides top and bottom by their greatest common divisor, found by the Euclidean algorithm, giving lowest terms. The applet only draws numbers up to 99, so after a big common denominator it asks you to simplify again; 97 and 89 give 8633, which is too big to draw. This page keeps that rule.

Try 3/4 and 6/8: the pictures look different but the status line says they are equal. Then try 97 and 89 as denominators and press Common denominator.
